Hi there! Ever wanted to run your PNGTuber natively in Vnyan? Well, now you can!
This logic loop will not work properly unless you configure a few things to support it. Here's what you'll need to get started. Important information is color coded with black nodes:

1. Import 4 "states" of pictures as props that your PNGTuber will use. 
	Currently the node blocks beside this one are set up to support states as follows:
	- TOP ROW: eyes closed and mouth open	- 2ND ROW: eyes open and mouth open
	- 3RD ROW: eyes closed mouth closed	- BOTTOM ROW: eyes open mouth closed

	*align the props to the world but do not lock them to always face the camera. You'll need to mess with the offest in the prop import menu to get placement just right.

2. Setup your mic input and number of active PNGTuber sets. You can do this by looking below this message box.

3. Setup your cameras.
	The first one can be whatever fits your placement best, and the second is a slightly more "zoomed in" version of the same camera. You will swap between these two cams when you speak to help give you PNGTuber a 	bit more life. By default, the nodegraph treats "Camera 1" as the idle camera and assumes you'll be situating your PNGTuber in the bottom right hand corner of the screen. "Camera 10" triggers when you are speaking, 	and assumes a camera placement that is slightly more zoomed in than "Camera 1"

	Below this message box are config options to configure the nodegraph to fit with your particular Vnyan setup. Your camera setup may differ and you may need to change the cameras specified.

4. Go to the settings menu and click on Misc (this is also where you can setup and save your camera). You'll need to setup a new position for your vtuber as we flatten and shrink it to serve as a source of colliders for other redeems.

	- Leave the default position slot as is, but go to slot Pos 1 and turn on the gizmo to move around your avatar's base coordinates.
	- You might have to zoom out to see the gizmo (it looks like the standard XYZ rotational sphere controls in blender).
	- Make sure to set it as "show" in the same menus you tweak your positions settings).
	- update all the Load Avatar node below this messgae box with your appropriate VTuber files. This is necessary for your PNGTuber to have collision
OPTIONAL STEP 5:

	- A node block is available below this one that allows you trigger transformations between different active PNGTubers! The triggers are set up to use websocket calls, but can be tweaked to suit your needs.
	- A node block is also available below this one that controls the transformation effect. It supports sound but you'll need to load your own files. It can also be tweaked as needed.
	- Another node block is available beside the other two that lets you specify specific effects to activate when specific PNGTubers are active. An experimental one is provided for you to try as an example.	- You can also set up a third camera to use with the <ScreenshotActive> parameter and as a zoomed in "close up" cam. 

Have fun! There's probably more I forgot, but these are the big ones. Let me know if you have questions and I'm happy to help, I'm best reached on Discord (Berymuch), but you can also message me on Bluesky :3

If you choose to use more than 4 different PNGTubers, you'll need to increase the value in the parameter filters to match the new value associated with that PNGTuber's "PNGberyloaded" parameter. In the case of a seventh PNGTuber, the value for "PNGberyloaded" would be 7.

[THIS PARAMETER IS VERY IMPORTANT]
Increase this parameter as you add more pngtubers. By default, it is configured to support up to 4 different PNGTubers. If you have less than 6 PNGTubers, reduce the range to match it to your amount. The count starts from 1. The value 0 is used when you want there to be no active PNGTubers. Start by setting up your first PNGTuber on the blue node block to the right as it is connected to <PNGberyloaded> = 1 value.

It is checked when someone redeems the PNGTuber and swaps the active PNGTuber to the one defined by the chosen parameter. It also checks to make sure not to give back the PNGTuber that is currently active. If a duplicate PNGTuber is rolled, it will randomize this parameter again until a non-duplicate is chosen.

The "PNGTuberMicTrigger" trigger logic runs to ensure that only the currently chosen PNGTuber graphics are being displayed as defined by the <PNGberyloaded> paramter. It also sends info to control PNG display states.It checks the parameter and hides the states associated with every other value greater than that parameter value. If the value is greater it then repeats this step until it reaches the specified parameter value. Any states that match the parameter are the ones that will be displayed.

Be default, 6 different  PNGTuber graphic sets are preconfigured. If you would like more than 6 possible states, check to see how the previous nodes are linked to properly set it up.

You can use these websocket commands to interface with your streamdeck or app of choice to trigger specific PNGTubers. The websocket command in black called "PNGZoomOn" lets you zoom in close with another camera if you set one up as a close up. The other websocket command called "PNGZoomOff" returns you to the neutral PNGTuber position. 

It is preconfigured to support 6 different PNGTubers.

Set the audio input to the microphone you would like to use.

You can control the sensitivity of voice detection by increasing or decreasing the volume value.

The two sound nodes below this message trigger every time the transformation effect starts. You will need to set this yourself if you would like to have a SFX

These SFX are randomly chosen from each time the transformation effect is triggered. I use these to randomize howls when my PNGTuber changes to spice it up a little.They will need to be configured by you if you choose to use them.
If you want your PNGTuber to have collision, you will need to load some form of VTuber here.

If you plan on using Channel points to let your viewers swap your PNGTuber, specify the name of the redeem here. You will have to create one with the exact same name on Twitch as well.
This node branch lets you set certain effects to trigger when specific PNGTubers are active. All you need to do is specify the value attached to the the "PNGberyloaded" variable to compare it to!
This controls the time it takes to do the transformation effect. Default value is 35.

These parameters control the following (1 is yes, 0 is no):
<PNGZoom>:
	Determines if the camera is currently zoomed in on the PNGTuber.
<PNGberyloaded>:
	Determines if a PNGTuber is currently active and which one. 0 is used when no PNGTuber is currently active.
<isspeaking>:
	Determines if you are currently beyond the mic threshold to trigger the speaking PNGTuber states.

<isblinking>:
	Determines if your PNGTuber is blinking.

<DuplicateCheck>:
	Compares with the last active PNGTuber and ensures selection randomization since the last time it was redeemed (available if the chat redeem 			is configured). This parameter is set by the last active <PNGberyloaded> parameter value.

<ScreenshotActive>: 
	Set to 1 to freeze your PNGTuber in its current state wherever camera 11 is set to be. you can change this under the setup box above.
You can set another camera here if you would like to have a close up cam. See the websocket node block below for info.

--------------------------------------------
V2.1 VNyan PNGTuber features:--------------------------------------------

- Fully documented with descriptive directions on how to configure and info on how 		parameters function.
- Supports 6+ different PNGTuber graphic sets (you can easily add more).

- Supports PNGTuber collision with all VNyan objects.

- Supports smart randomization of PNGTubers via chat redeem. It will remember 			which PNGTuber was used last and always give a different one on the next 		redeem usage.

- Supports zoom in on speaking.

- Supports randomized blinking.

- Supports websocket calls to trigger specific PNGTubers.

- Supports websocket call to activate a closeup view while maintaining expected 			PNGTuber behavior.

- Requires only VNyan to function with included logic for custom SFX.

- Supports a nifty graphical transformation effect when swapping between PNGTubers. 	This effect is also easily editable to suite your needs.

- Supports the triggering of custom graphical VNyan effects based on which 			PNGTuber is currently active.

- Lightweight and optimized!

- Easily tweaked and reconfigured to suit your needs.

- Includes an option to trigger a pause function for the currently active PNGTuber

- Designed by a wolf. UwU
You can change the range of time chosen from for the randomized blinking behavior. Values are in milliseconds.The default range is 125 to 8000

Connect the "Wait" node below to the BLUE "Parameter Filter" node near it to test effects to be loaded when the 1st PNGTuber is active.

I know it's a lot of node spaghetti, but this is the general idea of how it works and the things to consider when adding your 7th PNGTuber.

The toggle prop nodes that make your PNGTuber states visible are all connected to the associated trigger on the top left corner of the core logic node block. The toggle prop nodes that hide your PNGTuber states are all connected to those same triggers AND the parameter filter nodes above them for every other <PNGberyloaded> value.

If you add a 7th PNGTuber, you will need to not only do the above but also update every other PNGTuber Graphic state node block to toggle the states for the 7th one OFF using the parameter filters above the state triggers.
